transcript.text: Shark NZ801UK anti hair wrap upright - suction has gone really weak over the last couple of weeks, barely picks up crumbs. Have emptied the bin. Any ideas before I buy a new one?

It is very likely worth trying a fix before buying a new one. With your Shark NZ801UK, weak suction that develops gradually over weeks is almost always caused by clogged filters rather than a broken motor. Emptying the bin helps, but if the filters are saturated with fine dust and pet hair, they will choke the airflow even when the bin is empty. 1. Locate the pre-motor filter (usually near the top of the cyclone assembly) and the HEPA filter (often at the back or bottom). Wash them in cold water only—do not use detergent or put them in a dishwasher.
2. Shake out any loose hair from the filter mesh before washing.
3. Leave them to dry completely for at least 24 hours. Putting damp filters back in will severely reduce suction and can damage the motor. While they are drying, check the hose and wand by looking through them or running a long object (like a broom handle) through to ensure there is no blockage trapping crumbs. Once the filters are bone dry and reinstalled, try the vacuum again. If it remains weak after this, let me know.
[Helpful to see: image "Poor suction — what to check first" — Lost suction is usually a full bin, a dirty filter or a blockage in the hose, tube or floor head — check and clear those before suspecting the motor. Switch off and unplug first. Typical layout — your model may differ.]

Found the foam and felt filters under the bin, never washed them before. Washed in lukewarm water and dried them for 24 hours, and suction is back to like new. Hose and wand were clear too, and there's no burning smell.

That is excellent news. It was most likely the filters choking the airflow; washing them every few months keeps the suction strong and protects the motor from overheating. If you want to keep it running like this long-term, try giving the filters a quick rinse under cold water once a month or two, letting them dry fully before putting them back in. There is no need for any further checks or repairs.

reading.symptom: suction has gone really weak over the last couple of weeks, barely picks up crumbs

plan: They asked: "Any ideas before I buy a new one?" - answer that first.
Checks they have done and what they found: emptied the bin - done.
Already given by the customer, never ask for it again: make Shark; model NZ801UK.
The fault they reported is: "suction has gone really weak over the last couple of weeks, barely picks up crumbs". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.
The most likely cause, chosen from the evidence: a full bin or clogged filters. Lead with it and why it fits what they said; mention at most one alternative.

Stage 2: the checks they reported did not fix it. Give the next check that best separates the remaining likely causes, or say what the likely faulty part is if the checks already point to one. Until a check has confirmed which part has failed, name it as the likely part and the check that would confirm it; do not tell them to buy, order or replace it.
